title: Twenty First Word First Station Fifth Warning Two Spiritual Mines And The Loss Of Abandoning Prayer

questions.question: What is the first special gain a garden worker can get with a good intention?
questions.answer: The worker shares in the worship and praise made by the plants and trees.

questions.question: Which living things in the garden are included in that first gain?
questions.answer: Trees and plants with flowers or fruit are included.

questions.question: What is the second special gain from the garden produce?
questions.answer: Food taken from the garden can count like charity from the worker.

questions.question: Who may eat from the garden and still make that reward happen?
questions.answer: People, animals, bugs, buyers, and even thieves.

questions.question: What must the worker do so the garden work becomes like charity?
questions.answer: Work for Allah, stay within what Allah allows, and know the goods belong to Allah.

questions.question: How should the worker think about his job in the garden?
questions.answer: He should see himself as someone handing out Allah’s gifts to His creatures.

questions.question: What does a person lose by leaving the required prayers?
questions.answer: The person loses great reward and misses the two special gains.

questions.question: How can missing prayer hurt a person’s feelings about work later in life?
questions.answer: The person may get tired of the work, stop caring, and become lazy.

questions.question: Why does the praying person keep working with energy?
questions.answer: He hopes for more light for the grave and more provision for the next life.

questions.question: What two kinds of work does the hopeful person want to do more of?
questions.answer: Worship and lawful daily work.

questions.question: In the passage, what makes a person receive reward from the plants and trees?
questions.answer: Having a sincere and sound intention.

questions.question: Does the first reward come only from fruit trees? Name the kinds mentioned.
questions.answer: No. It comes from both flowering and fruit-bearing plants and trees.

questions.question: If garden food is eaten, what can it become for the worker?
questions.answer: It can become like giving charity.

questions.question: Which is needed for that reward: any kind of work, or work done in Allah’s name and in a halal way?
questions.answer: Work done in Allah’s name and in a halal way.

questions.question: Why is it important to remember that the garden goods belong to Allah?
questions.answer: It helps the worker stay humble and act like a helper, not an owner over everything.

questions.question: What big mistake does the passage warn about when someone leaves the daily prayers?
questions.answer: That person throws away great reward and misses valuable blessings.

questions.question: What kind of thoughts may an older person have after leaving prayer for a long time?
questions.answer: The person may think the work is not worth it because life in this world will end anyway.

questions.question: What bad habit can grow from those thoughts?
questions.answer: Idleness and not wanting to work.

questions.question: What does the better person hope to send ahead by working harder?
questions.answer: More light for the grave and more supplies for the hereafter.

questions.question: What is one reward for a gardener who works with the right purpose in the heart?
questions.answer: The gardener gets a share in the remembrance and praise done by the garden’s plants and trees.

questions.question: What part of the garden is talked about in that reward?
questions.answer: The growing plants and trees, including ones with blossoms and fruits.

questions.question: When food from the garden is taken, what good deed can it be counted as?
questions.answer: It can be counted like charity.

questions.question: Name two groups from the passage that may take the produce.
questions.answer: Buyers and thieves.

questions.question: What three things are needed for the produce to count that way?
questions.answer: A person must work for Allah, stay inside Allah’s allowed limits, and see himself as passing out Allah’s property.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about who truly owns the garden goods?
questions.answer: Allah is the true Owner.

questions.question: How does skipping prayer affect eagerness for work?
questions.answer: It takes away strong drive and weakens courage and cheer.

questions.question: What may the non-praying person say about leaving this world?
questions.answer: He may say that he is going away anyway, so the hard work feels pointless.

questions.question: What is different about the person who prays?
questions.answer: He wants to do more worship and halal work for reward in the life to come.

questions.question: What does a good intention do for someone working in a garden?
questions.answer: It brings reward from the worship of the plants and trees.

questions.question: Are only people mentioned in the second reward from the garden produce?
questions.answer: No. Animals, insects, buyers, and thieves are mentioned too.

questions.question: Why can even food taken by others still bring reward?
questions.answer: Because it may count like charity for the worker.

questions.question: What condition about Allah must the worker remember while working?
questions.answer: The worker must remember Allah is the True Provider.

questions.question: What condition about rules must the worker follow?
questions.answer: The worker must stay within what Allah permits.

questions.question: If a person leaves the prescribed prayers, what two treasures are lost?
questions.answer: The two special gains from the garden work are lost.

questions.question: How does the passage describe that loss?
questions.answer: It is a huge loss, like becoming bankrupt.

questions.question: What may happen when that person gets older?
questions.answer: He may become worn out and stop caring about gardening.

questions.question: What feeling can replace effort in that person?
questions.answer: Laziness can replace effort.

questions.question: What makes the first man keep striving?
questions.answer: He wants reward for the grave and the hereafter, so he works more in worship and lawful jobs.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the first “mine,” or treasure, from garden work?
questions.answer: A share in the worshipful praise made by the garden’s plants and trees.

questions.question: What kind of intention is needed for that treasure?
questions.answer: A right and sincere intention.

questions.question: What is the second “mine,” or treasure?
questions.answer: The garden produce being counted like charity when it is eaten.

questions.question: Is that reward only when honest buyers take it, or also when others take it?
questions.answer: Also when others take it, even thieves.

questions.question: What should a worker think about his place when giving out the garden goods?
questions.answer: He should think of himself as a servant delivering Allah’s gifts.

questions.question: What happens to a person’s inner strength when prayer is abandoned?
questions.answer: The person loses strong spirit and encouragement.

questions.question: What idea makes the tired person stop caring about the work?
questions.answer: Thinking that he will leave the world soon anyway.

questions.question: What does that wrong thinking lead to?
questions.answer: It leads to laziness and giving up.

questions.question: What is the hopeful person trying to gather for later?
questions.answer: Reward, light for the grave, and provision for the next life.

questions.question: What reward comes from the garden itself when a person works with a proper intention?
questions.answer: The person gets reward connected to the praising of Allah by the plants and trees.

questions.question: What kinds of plants are named in the passage?
questions.answer: Ones with blossoms and ones that bear fruit.

questions.question: What can happen when garden food is eaten by any creature or person named there?
questions.answer: It can be counted as charity for the worker.

questions.question: Give one example of a creature and one example of a person from the passage who may take the produce.
questions.answer: A fly and a buyer.

questions.question: What makes that reward possible besides just planting and harvesting?
questions.answer: Working for Allah, obeying His limits, and knowing the goods are His.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the person who stops the required prayers?
questions.answer: That person loses great reward and misses two valuable sources of benefit.

questions.question: How is that loss compared to money matters?
questions.answer: It is like ending up bankrupt.

questions.question: What may happen to that person’s attitude toward gardening in old age?
questions.answer: The person may become tired of it and not want to continue.

questions.question: What question may that person ask to show loss of purpose?
questions.answer: He may wonder why he should go on with such hardship if he will leave the world.

questions.question: What goal gives the praying person more energy for work?
questions.answer: Wanting more reward for the grave and the hereafter.
